title: Why Do We Make Plans We Never KEEP?
title_alternatives: Why Your Plans FAIL (And What Science Says)
Your Brain Thinks Future You Is a STRANGER
The 30% Problem: Why We Never FINISH on Time
You're Not Lazy. Your Plans Are BROKEN
description:
Sunday night you write the perfect plan. By Wednesday it's gone. Only about 30% of students in a classic study finished on time, and brain scans suggest we treat our future selves like strangers. Here's why plans fail, and the one simple if-then trick that works across dozens of studies.

This video is psychology for education, not medical or professional advice.

- Webb & Sheeran (2006). Does changing behavioral intentions engender behavior change? Psychological Bulletin.
- Hershfield et al. (2011). Neural measures of future self-continuity predict temporal discounting.
- Steel (2007). The nature of procrastination. Psychological Bulletin.

- Milne, Orbell & Sheeran (2002). British Journal of Health Psychology.
- Sydney Opera House history (Flyvbjerg; ArchDaily; Classical Music).
